gloss: to lend a hand; to help out

definitions.gloss: to lend a hand; to help out
definitions.explanation: To offer practical assistance to someone with a task or problem.

examples.japanese: ちょっと{手|て}を{貸|か}して。
examples.english: Give me a hand for a sec.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{時|とき}に{友人|ゆうじん}が{手|て}を{貸|か}してくれた。
examples.english: A friend helped me out when I was moving.

examples.japanese: {困|こま}っている{人|ひと}がいたら、{手|て}を{貸|か}すのは{当然|とうぜん}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think it's only natural to lend a hand when someone is in trouble.

notes:
An idiomatic expression meaning to offer help, literally "to lend one's hand." It implies physical or practical assistance rather than emotional support. Often used in casual requests.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手|て}を{貸|か}してください: please help me (polite)
- {手|て}を{貸|か}してくれる: to help out (for me)
- {手|て}を{貸|か}してもらう: to have someone help

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手伝|てつだ}う: to help — a more general verb for helping; {手|て}を{貸|か}す emphasizes lending brief, practical assistance
- {力|ちから}を{貸|か}す: to lend one's strength — similar idiom but implies stronger or more sustained support
- {助|たす}ける: to rescue, to save — used for more urgent or serious situations
